findings.title: Queries get interpolated multiple times when shard splitting delegates to runSplitQuery
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery() now interpolates every target with datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters) before any splitting happens (lines 49-53). However, splitQueriesByStreamShard()'s runNextRequest() (shardQuerySplitting.ts, ~line 163) calls runSplitQuery(datasource, subRequest, options) once per shard group/cycle, and runSplitQuery() (querySplitting.ts, lines 296-299) now also unconditionally re-interpolates request.targets via datasource.applyTemplateVariables for every call. Because the sub-request built for each shard group still carries the already-interpolated (and shard-selector-modified) targets, those targets get interpolated again on every shard cycle. This is confirmed by the updated test expectation in shardQuerySplitting.test.ts ('Interpolates queries before running') which changed from `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` to `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` for a single logical query split into 4 shard groups. Repeated interpolation is wasteful, and if applyTemplateVariables is not idempotent (e.g. it injects ad hoc filters as extra label matchers into the selector text, as its own test mock does by mutating query.expr), running it multiple times on the same query risks duplicating ad hoc filter clauses or otherwise corrupting the final selector sent to the backend when ad hoc filters (request.filters) are present.

findings.title: Moving interpolation before querySupportsSplitting() defeats the $__range splitting safeguard
findings.body: querySupportsSplitting() (lines 282-289) relies on isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr) to detect queries using the $__range family of variables, with the comment explaining that such queries must not be time-split because the interpolated $__range value would otherwise become incorrect. Previously this check ran on the raw (non-interpolated) expr, so the literal '$__range' text was still present and detectable. Now queries are interpolated via datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...) at line 299 before this check runs at line 300, so by the time isQueryWithRangeVariable() executes, any '$__range' reference has already been replaced with its literal value and can no longer be detected in the string. As a result, querySupportsSplitting() can never classify a query as using $__range anymore, so such queries will now flow into the normal time-splitting path (logQueries/metricQueries) instead of being executed as a single non-split request, risking incorrect merged results for queries that depend on $__range spanning the whole original range versus the narrower per-partition sub-ranges. The accompanying comment is now also stale/misleading since the described protection no longer functions as written.

findings.title: No regression test for $__range queries after reordering interpolation and splitting checks
findings.body: The PR reorders interpolation to happen before querySupportsSplitting()/isQueryWithRangeVariable() is evaluated (see querySplitting.ts), which changes whether queries using the $__range variable get excluded from time splitting. No test was added (here or elsewhere in this file) that exercises a query containing $__range to confirm it is still correctly excluded from splitting, or to validate the new intended behavior if inclusion is now considered safe. Given this is exactly the kind of interaction the interpolation-timing change affects, its absence leaves a meaningful regression risk unverified.

findings.title: No test verifies ad hoc filters aren't duplicated due to repeated interpolation
findings.body: The test 'Interpolates queries before running' now asserts datasource.applyTemplateVariables is called 5 times for a single query (previously the batch call interpolateVariablesInQueries was asserted to run once), confirming the query gets interpolated multiple times across the shard-splitting/time-splitting delegation. None of the tests pass a non-empty request.filters (ad hoc filters) to verify that this repeated interpolation does not duplicate ad hoc filter matchers in the final query selector sent to runQuery. Given applyTemplateVariables is the mechanism typically used to inject ad hoc filters into the query text, and it is now invoked multiple times per logical query, this scenario should be covered by a dedicated test.
